note: Frozen budgets for the shell elements. Measured on 2026-09-14 on the CPU float64 backend. The corrugated tube is the reason the shell exists: a pleated wall must open by unfolding, not by stretching its material, because a gut that reaches 80 cm by stretching would need twelve times its circumference in material strain and would thin to foil. Written before the measurement, then set from it.

corrugated_tube.geometry: 16 pleats around, 9 rings along, pleat amplitude 0.008 m on a 0.02 m mean radius, opened by a growing capsule bolus over 200 steps and settled for 200 more

radius_growth.note: lower bound. The lumen must actually open, or the test proves nothing.

area_growth.note: upper bound, and the point of the whole element type. The measurement is 0.000 to six figures: the pleats unfold and the material does not stretch at all. A fraction of a percent is allowed for the settling motion; anything above that means the wall is stretching and the shell is buying nothing over a tet wall.
